# Skill: graphql-generation

## Purpose

Define GraphQL queries and mutations and generate typed Dart code using **Ferry**. Unlike chopper, there is no separate abstract service interface — the service class interacts directly with the GraphQL client to execute requests.

---

## Code Generation Command

```bash
python3 scripts/build.py graphql
```

Run this after creating or modifying any `.graphql` file. It generates `__generated__/` files (`.data.gql.dart`, `.req.gql.dart`, `.var.gql.dart`) alongside the source.

---

## File Structure

```
lib/infrastructure/<feature>/service/graphql/
├── <operation_name>.graphql            ← you write this
├── __generated__/                      ← generated by Ferry
│   ├── <operation_name>.data.gql.dart
│   ├── <operation_name>.req.gql.dart
│   └── <operation_name>.var.gql.dart
```

The shared schema lives at:

```
lib/infrastructure/core/graphql/schema/schema.graphql
```

---

## Writing a Query

```graphql
query SearchBanks($swift: String, $name: String) {
  searchBanks(swift: $swift, name: $name) {
    ... on ForeignBankInfoList {
      banks {
        swift
        name
        city
        country
      }
    }
    ... on ValidationError {
      message
      code
    }
    ... on UnexpectedError {
      message
      code
    }
  }
}
```

---

## Writing a Mutation

```graphql
mutation UpdateKnownForeignRecipient($knownForeignRecipient: KnownForeignRecipientUpdateInput!) {
  knownForeignRecipientUpdate(knownForeignRecipient: $knownForeignRecipient) {
    ... on KnownForeignRecipientsChangeSuccess {
      id
    }
    ... on ValidationError {
      message
      code
    }
    ... on UnexpectedError {
      message
      code
    }
  }
}
```

---

## Service Class Pattern

Services use the generated request/data/vars types directly against the GraphQL client:

```dart
import 'package:ferry/ferry.dart';
import 'package:injectable/injectable.dart';
import 'package:isbapp/domain/core/value_objects/payload.dart';
import 'package:isbapp/infrastructure/core/graphql/base_graphql_service.dart';
import 'package:isbapp/infrastructure/core/graphql/i_graphql_client_provider.dart';
import 'package:isbapp/infrastructure/<feature>/service/graphql/__generated__/<operation>.data.gql.dart';
import 'package:isbapp/infrastructure/<feature>/service/graphql/__generated__/<operation>.req.gql.dart';
import 'package:isbapp/infrastructure/<feature>/service/graphql/__generated__/<operation>.var.gql.dart';

@InjectableEnv.online
@LazySingleton(as: I<Feature>Service)
class <Feature>Service extends BaseGraphQLService implements I<Feature>Service {
  final IGraphqlClientProvider _gqClientProvider;

  <Feature>Service(this._gqClientProvider);

  @override
  Future<Payload<ResponseModel>> getData({int level = 1}) async {
    try {
      final G<Operation>Req request = G<Operation>Req(
        (G<Operation>ReqBuilder b) => b..vars.param = value,
      );

      final Stream<OperationResponse<G<Operation>Data, G<Operation>Vars>> stream =
          _gqClientProvider.getClient().request(request);
      final OperationResponse<G<Operation>Data, G<Operation>Vars> response =
          await stream.first;

      if (await needsRetry(response, level)) {
        return getData(level: level + 1);
      }

      return handleResponse(
        response,
        (G<Operation>Data data) => ResponseModel.fromGraphQL(data),
      );
    } on Exception catch (e, stacktrace) {
      return handleException(e, stacktrace);
    }
  }
}
```

### Alternative: Feature-specific client provider

Some features use a dedicated `IClientProvider` that exposes both `getClient()` (HTTP) and `getGraphQLClient()`:

```dart
class <Feature>Service with BaseService implements I<Feature>Service {
  final I<Feature>ClientProvider _clientProvider;

  // ...
  _clientProvider.getGraphQLClient().request(request);
}
```

---

## Union Type Handling

GraphQL union/interface responses generate typed subtypes. Handle them with `is` checks:

```dart
final G<Operation>Data_<field>? result = response.data?.<field>;

if (result is G<Operation>Data_<field>__asSuccessType) {
  // extract data
}
if (result is G<Operation>Data_<field>__asValidationError) {
  return Payload.failure(Failure.invalidValue(message: result.message));
}
if (result is G<Operation>Data_<field>__asUnexpectedError) {
  return Payload.failure(Failure.graphQLError(message: result.message));
}
```

---

## Base Classes

| Class | Role |
|-------|------|
| `BaseGraphQLService` | Provides `needsRetry()`, `handleResponse()`, `handleException()` — use for services with `IGraphqlClientProvider` |
| `BaseService` | Provides `needsRetryGraphQL()`, `handleException()` — use as mixin for services with feature-specific client providers |
| `BaseGraphQlClient` | Ferry client wrapper; use `isGraphQLResponseSuccess()` and `getErrors()` for manual checks |

---

## Rules

| Rule | Detail |
|------|--------|
| One operation per `.graphql` file | Name file after the operation (snake_case) |
| Operation naming | `PascalCase` matching the GraphQL operation name |
| Variables | Use `$variableName` in the query, map to vars builder in Dart |
| Error union fragments | Always include `... on ValidationError`, `... on UnexpectedError`, and any domain-specific error types |
| FetchPolicy | Default is `FetchPolicy.NetworkOnly`; set explicitly if needed |
| Schema types | Use types from `schema.graphql`; do not redefine them |
| Retry pattern | Use `needsRetry(response, level)` with `level` parameter for 401 retries |

---

## What NOT to Do

- Do not manually write the `__generated__/` files — run the build command
- Do not import domain layer classes in the service (exception: `Payload`, `Failure`)
- Do not duplicate schema types in `.graphql` files
- Do not skip error union variants — always handle all possible return types
- Do not use `FetchPolicy.CacheFirst` unless explicitly required
